$comment: Pragmatic refactoring policy for loop-refactorer (v2: general, project-agnostic metrics). Tighten the numbers here later; the agent reads them every round.

routine.$comment: in the build loop after every N accepted features: a little order, every time

clean.$comment: on demand when the alarm values are reached

stop.$comment: stop after 2 consecutive steps without any metric gain, or after 2 steps reverted because tests turned red

targets.$comment: cognitiveMax: SonarSource default is 15; 10 keeps every function easy to read. duplicationPct over JS, CSS and HTML.

hotspotFirst: Within a metric, start in the file with the highest hotspot score (changes × size, see code-metrics hotspots): refactoring pays off where code is both big and often changed.

alarm.$comment: after a routine round: if any value is at or above its alarm value, the loop recommends a clean run

boyScout: If every target is met: do exactly ONE step — the most obvious local cleanup in the top hotspot file (e.g. lower the cognitive complexity of its most complex function, extract a duplicated block, clarify one name). No cross-module renames, no restructuring. Then stop with stopReason 'boy-scout'.
